previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and alcohol abuse, was admitted with chest pain and hemoptysis. A CT scan revealed an acute pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe with associated pulmonary infarct and pleural effusion. He was started on anticoagulation with Lovenox and prescribed Coumadin for long-term management, with Pradaxa and aspirin discontinued. Despite clear explanation of the life-threatening risks, he chose to leave against medical advice. At discharge, he was alert, oriented, and demonstrated understanding of his treatment plan, including medication instructions and the need for INR monitoring. He was sent home with prescriptions and strict instructions to avoid alcohol and seek immediate care for worsening symptoms.

He also states that he has no other compliants or concerns at

In the ED on ___, the patient requested to leave after 
complaining of chest pain. He then stayed for altered MS 
secondary to benzos. He left AMA, then came back, vomited blood 
and felt dizzy. CT revealed +PE, and hep gtt was started. He had 
agreed to stay in hospital and get admitted. On the floor, he 
was obviously intoxicated as he was much more drowsy and not 
answering questions. It was decided that we would give the pt 
time to wake up, detoxify and then re-address questions with 
him. However, he then insisted on leaving again, but was not 
allowed to given his intoxication. He then began raising his 
voice and making threatening remarks to the staff. Security and 
psychiatry were called. He was given 5mg IV haldol and 2mg IV 
ativan when pt would not cooperate and he was put in leather 
restraints. When he was more with it, he continued to insist on 
leaving and the team instructed him that he needed to pick up 
his prescription for enoxaparin at the pharmacy or he could die. 
 
  
He now returns once again to the ED, appearing intoxicated. 
Initial vitals were: 96.4 77 132/71 14 98% 3L NC.

He admitted to alcohol usage in the ER.  
He was given a dose of Lovenox 40 mg SC x1 and Hgb was noted to 
be stable at 9. He had not filled the lovenox prescription given 
to him.  
ECG was performed with significant baseline artifact that 
appeared similar to prior, ? lead misplacement given V5 
morphology.  
Serum tox was positive for benzos. Coags and chemistry panel 
were similar to prior.  
On the floor, patient was initially burrowed into a layer of 
covers. After turning on the light, he appeared from under the 
covers and looked quite fatigue. He denies any chest pain. His 
main concern is letting his sister know that he is in the

Brief Hospital Course:
___ history of chronic systolic heart failure (35% per ECHO) s/p 
AICD placement, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and alcohol 
abuse who presents with hemoptysis and chest pain found to have 
PE. He is now re-admitted after leaving AMA the prior day.  
 
ACUTE ISSUES 
# Pulmonary Embolism - Chest angiography revealing pulmonary 
embolism in basal segment of right lower lobe with adjacent 
opacity with likely pulmonary infarct. There was no evidence of 
right heart strain. Patient representing after leaving AMA after 
realizing that continuing chest pain was from blood clot in lung 
that needed treatment. He is hemodynamically stable, no evidence 
of clot burden in leg. Etiology of pulmonary embolism uncertain 
- difficult to ascertain comprehensive history given fatigued. 
He was continued on systemic anticoagulation with enoxaparin. 
Patient has normal renal function, not obese, no indication for 
anti-Xa monitoring. He was also continued on warfarin 5mg daily 
with the plan for adequate bridging to occur prior to 
discontinuing lovenox. However, pt again wanted to leave against 
medical advice. He voiced the understanding that if he left the 
hospital without appropriate treatment and adequate follow-up, 
he could die. He understood this and chose to leave against 
medical advice anyway. He was not provided with lovenox 
injections this time, as he had proven that he cannot take care 
of this medication since he had lost the syringes after being 
provided the medication yesterday. It was deemed more dangerous 
than safe for him to be discharged on new blood thinners, so he 
was not discharged on coumadin (or lovenox), given the high risk 
of bleeding in combination with the high-risk of falls that he 
would be likely subjected to, given his addiction to 
benzodiazepines and alcohol. 
 
# Pleural effusion,right - Recent chest imaging showing small to 
moderate right pleural effusion, likely ___ PE.  

CHRONIC ISSUES
# Substance abuse - Patient has history of alcohol abuse, and he 
reports last drink was yesterday (only 0.5 can per his reports). 
Serum tox screen is positive for benzos as was positive on his 
admission yesterday, however was given 2mg IV ativan yesterday 
morning while in-house. He currently appears intoxicated but 
AAOx3 and arousable to voice. Psychiatry was consulted, given 
his desire to leave against medical advice while being 
intoxicated. It was deemed that pt was no longer intoxicated and 
voiced an understanding of the situation and the consequences of 
leaving the hospital without treatment. Pt could not be held 
against his will given his adequate capacity, and so left 
against medical advice (as above). He was put on CIWA, with 
valium 5mg for CIWA > 10, though did not score, and his home 
Campral was held while in-house. His home prilosec was held for 
likely alcoholic gastritis (and GERD).    

# Atrial Fibrillation - He appeared to be in sinus tachycardia 
on admission. He was continued on systemic anticoagulation 
(lovenox and coumadin) as above, and was continued on 
rate-control with metoprolol.    
 
# Chronic Systolic Heart Failure - Patient has EF documented of 
16% on last nuclear stress test, but ECHO a few days after 
stress test, documents 35%. On lasix and metoprolol at home. He 
was continued on his home metoprolol, losartan, and lasix while 
in-house during this admission.    
 
# HTN - Pt was continued on his home metoprolol, losartan.  
  
# HL - Pt was continued on his home simvastatin.
